discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 010619
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
119 AM EST Sun Nov 1 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Mostly cloudy today but remaining mild with highs well into
  the 60s and perhaps low 70s. 

- Very warm on Tuesday and breezy followed by increasing rain 
  chances through Wednesday (60% chance).

- Rain showers may linger at times into Thursday and Friday, 
  with highs near 60.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 116 AM EST Sun Nov 1 2026

A trough working its way through the mid-Missippi valley today 
brings plenty of clouds to our local area while the best rain chance 
associated with this features resides outside of our forecast area 
to the south. I did carry 10% POPs for the day in preparation for 
any rogue sprinkles in this period of continued, weak WAA and ascent.

Rain chances increase in the days ahead as the 500-mb pattern 
becomes highly amplified due to a deep trough emerging from the 
Rockies. Gulf moisture seeps in atop a mid-Atlantic ridge, perhaps 
leading to isoalted showers Monday afternoon. Low confidence on this 
as the best moisture pooling is off to the west, yet available CAMs 
do litter portions of the area with isolated showers. Very warm and 
breezy Tuesday as one low occludes over the UP and cyclogenesis 
renews over the Central Plains. We'll see high temperatures soar 
well into the 70s (challenging records) depending on cloud cover. 
Similarly, the magnitude of any synoptic wind gusts will hinge on 
breaks in the clouds aiding to mix down a strengthening low-level 
jet. Poor lapse rates and a lack of instability look to keep the 
severe weather risk in check Wednesday as the occluded front moves 
through in the first half of the day. With the low lingering over 
the Midwest Thursday, breezy conditions may persist while rain 
chances pause within the dry slot of this expansive system. 

Not a ton of cold air behind this low with ridging noted in the Lee 
of the Rockies. The result is high temperatures to finish out the 
week right near 60 with lows near 40. Low shower chances may persist 
through the end of the week until the low finally exits over the 
Northeast. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z MONDAY/...
Issued at 1245 AM EDT Sun Nov 1 2026

A trough passing south of the Ohio Valley brings plenty of
clouds to the local area, but generally expected to be rain-
free. Modest WAA could squeeze out a rogue shower or sprinkle, 
but high resolution ensembles generally paint this as less than 
a 20% chance. Wind less than 10 knots through the period.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

spc.text:
SPC AC 010607

   Day 1 Convective Outlook CORR 1
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0107 AM CDT Sun Nov 01 2026

   Valid 011200Z - 021200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS...

   CORRECTED FOR WORDING

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms associated with severe wind gusts and a tornado threat
   are expected this evening into tonight from parts of New Mexico
   northeastward into the southern High Plains. A more isolated severe
   threat will be possible in parts of the Desert Southwest this
   afternoon.

   ...Desert Southwest/Southern Rockies/Southern High Plains...
   A mid-level shortwave trough will move across California into the
   Desert Southwest today. Ahead of the system, a sufficiently moist
   airmass will be in place across parts of southern and central
   Arizona, where scattered thunderstorms will develop during the
   afternoon. Large-scale ascent and strong deep-layer shear will
   support an isolated severe threat with cells that initiate and
   develop within weak instability. Supercells with potential for
   isolated severe wind gusts will be possible as a larger-scale band
   of storms becomes more well-defined.

   Ahead of this convective band, moisture advection will take place
   today in the southern High Plains of eastern New Mexico and west
   Texas. Surface dewpoints will gradually increase into the lower to
   mid 60s F. Along and near the moist axis, moderate instability will
   develop in the late afternoon and early evening. The large-scale
   line segment is expected to become increasingly organized as it
   approaches the instability axis. The potential for severe wind gusts
   and a few tornadoes will likely become maximized as the line moves
   through the stronger instability this evening over eastern New
   Mexico and west Texas.

   RAP forecast soundings this evening from Roswell, NM northward to
   Clovis, NM have 0-6 km shear in the 55 to 65 knot range with some
   veering winds with height and substantial low-level speed shear. 0-3
   km storm-relative helicity is forecast to reach the 250 to 350 m2/s2
   range in parts of eastern New Mexico in the early to mid evening.
   This will support a tornado threat with supercells that form within
   the large-scale band. Severe wind gusts will also be possible with
   the more intense parts of the line segment. Severe wind gusts above
   70 knots may occur with the faster-moving bowing structures. The
   severe threat may continue into the overnight period as the line
   moves northeastward into northwest Oklahoma and southern Kansas.

   ..Broyles/Weinman.. 11/01/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.summary: Scattered severe storms are expected across parts of the central and southern Plains late Monday afternoon into the evening, with damaging wind gusts and a few tornadoes the main threats.
spc.text:
SPC AC 010602

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0102 AM CDT Sun Nov 01 2026

   Valid 021200Z - 031200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER MUCH OF
   OKLAHOMA...NORTHERN TEXAS...AND SOUTH-CENTRAL AND EASTERN KANSAS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered severe storms are expected across parts of the central and
   southern Plains late Monday afternoon into the evening, with
   damaging wind gusts and a few tornadoes the main threats.

   ...Synopsis...
   A deep upper trough will move out of the Rockies and into the
   Plains, with a leading speed max moving swiftly across western TX
   and toward the MO Valley during the day. Meanwhile, a stronger speed
   max will move across NM and into KS, OK, and northwest TX by late in
   the day, and across the remainder of KS and OK overnight.

   A surface low will deepen across central NE, with a cold front
   moving into western NE and KS. A dryline will extend roughly from
   central KS into western OK and west-central TX by 00Z, with mid 60s
   F dewpoints across the warm sector. A 50-60 kt southerly low-level
   jet will develop late in the day into the overnight period, also
   aiding northward advection of moisture. At least a narrow zone of
   supercell potential is evident near the dryline late in the day,
   with a few tornadoes and damaging wind possible. The severe risk
   should persist through the late evening with damaging winds and
   possible QLCS storm mode, along with an isolated tornado risk.

   ...Parts of northern TX across OK and into eastern KS...
   Capping due to relatively cool boundary-layer temperatures will
   inhibit storms for much of the day, with a zone of steeper low-level
   lapse rates near the dryline. Initial cell development is expected
   there, from south-central KS into western OK and northwest TX after
   21Z, with increasing coverage of storms through the evening as the
   system continues eastward. Effective SRH of 200-300 m2/s2 will be
   common, though effectiveness away from the dryline will depend on
   how warm the boundary layer becomes. At the very least, initial
   cells would appear to have a tornado risk, with sufficient
   instability of 1000-1500 J/kg. A conditional risk of an EF2 tornado
   exists due to favorable shear, and depending on destabilization.
   Storms may become more linear with time as they move across OK,
   north TX and eastern KS, with decreasing instability after 06Z.

   ..Jewell.. 11/01/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.summary: Scattered storms will occur from the Sabine and Lower Mississippi Valleys northward into the Mid Mississippi Valley on Tuesday. A few thunderstorms may produce damaging gusts.
spc.text:
SPC AC 010832

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0232 AM CST Sun Nov 01 2026

   Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER PARTS OF
   THE LOWER TO MIDDLE MISSISSIPPI VALLEY AND TOWARD THE SABINE
   RIVER...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered storms will occur from the Sabine and Lower Mississippi
   Valleys northward into the Mid Mississippi Valley on Tuesday. A few
   thunderstorms may produce damaging gusts.

   ...Discussion...
   On Tuesday, an amplified upper trough will move east out of the
   Plains and toward the MS Valley, with an expansive region of
   south/southwest winds aloft from the Sabine Valley to the Upper
   Great Lakes. Southerly surface winds will further transport moisture
   northward with 60s F dewpoints to the Mid MS Valley, and upper 60s F
   into the Lower MS Valley. 

   The elongated surface trough/wind shift will support rain and
   thunderstorms through the period as the trough gradually shifts
   east. Some diurnal increase in storm intensity is possible, and the
   greatest potential for isolated severe storms should be over
   southern parts of the MS Valley and to the Sabine River where
   instability will be strongest. Wind profiles will be marginally
   supportive of severe storms with 30-35 kt effective shear over
   southern areas. Farther north into MO and IL, shear will be
   stronger, but instability will be quite weak. Strong wind gusts
   appear to be the main threat.

   ..Jewell.. 11/01/2026

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 3 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1930Z

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
